name: Driftwood Testimony
description:
A raw, sprawling double-album compiled by an anonymous collective operating out of Tier 1's flooded eastern wards, released in 2191 on water-damaged data chips and pirate neural feeds. Fourteen artists contributed tracks — some established, most unknown — recorded in basements, drainage corridors, and the back rooms of unlicensed pharmacies. The production is deliberately rough: field recordings bleed into vocals, power fluctuations leave audible artifacts, and at least three tracks feature the distant sound of Vantablack Security drones passing overhead mid-recording. The album circulated for eight months before corporate censors identified it, by which point an estimated 400,000 copies had propagated across the Shelf's mesh networks.

Standout tracks include 'Rent Meridian,' a slow, grinding piece by Yemisi Strand-Kowalczyk that layers kora-derived fingerpicking against a mechanical pulse and a spoken-word accounting of a Tier 1 eviction notice read verbatim. 'Flood Protocol (We Were Not Warned)' by an artist identified only as NKOSI features West African polyrhythm percussion built entirely from industrial salvage, with a vocal melody drawn from a Scandinavian lament tradition — the combination is haunting and furious in equal measure. The final track, 'Address Unknown,' is eighteen minutes of ambient drone that slowly incorporates recordings of Shelf residents speaking their former addresses before displacement — a document as much as a song.
creator: The Driftwood Collective (anonymous)
genre: Shelf Protest / Industrial Folk / Ambient Documentary
audience: Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents, labor organizers, underground journalists, activist networks
cultural_impact: Driftwood Testimony became the defining protest record of the 2190s Shelf displacement crisis, when Vantablack Infrastructure demolished three eastern wards to expand cooling infrastructure for Spire data centers. The album's circulation — unstoppable despite corporate suppression — demonstrated that physical media distribution networks were more resilient than neural feed censorship. Two of the contributing artists were later detained under the GLMZ Cultural Disruption Ordinance, which only accelerated the album's mythological status. Copies of the original data chips now trade for Φ800-2,000 on gray markets.
story_hooks: A player character finds an original data chip embedded in the wall of a building scheduled for demolition — the chip contains an eighteenth track never included in the distributed version, featuring a voice that matches a high-ranking Vantablack executive.

The anonymous NKOSI has resurfaced after years of silence and wants to record a follow-up, but needs the players to secure a safe recording location and protect the sessions from corporate surveillance.

A Vantablack legal team is quietly offering significant sums to anyone who can identify the Driftwood Collective's core organizers — some Shelf residents are tempted, others are furious, and the community is fracturing.
